citation.sourceDocument: Indiana DOR Rates, Fees & Penalties — 2.95% adjusted gross income tax for 2026 (2.90% in 2027); $1,000 personal exemption
citation.sourceNote: Indiana's flat adjusted-gross-income tax is on a statutory glide path down (HEA 1001, 2023): the DOR's rates page states it directly — 'The Indiana Individual adjusted gross income tax rate for 2026 is 2.95% and will adjust in 2027 to 2.90%.' (2025 was 3.00%.) There is no Indiana standard deduction; the relief is a $1,000-per-taxpayer personal exemption (IC 6-3-1-3.5), so $1,000 single and head of household, $2,000 married filing jointly. Worked example, single $60,000: taxable = 60,000 − 1,000 = $59,000; tax = 2.95%·59,000 = $1,740.50. The significant omission is INDIANA COUNTY INCOME TAX. Every one of the 92 counties levies its own rate — roughly 0.5% to over 3% — on residents, and unlike Maryland's county tax (which this engine models as a mandatory residence-based selection) Indiana's counties are not seeded here, so a real Indiana filer owes meaningfully more than the figure shown. The $1,000 dependent exemption and the additional $1,500 first-year-dependent and age-65/blind exemptions are omitted too, as is the county rate chart in Departmental Notice #1. Verified against the Indiana DOR rates page on 2026-08-29.
